subject: Chemistry
description: Covers Baking soda, Bronze, and Detergents.

questions.stem: What is the chemical name of common 'Baking Soda' used in kitchens to make cakes and bread fluffy?

options.option_text: Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3)
Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3)
Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)
Calcium hypochlorite (Ca(OCl)2)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Baking soda is Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO3). When baking soda is mixed with a mild edible acid (like tartaric acid to make 'baking powder') and heated, it undergoes a chemical reaction that releases Carbon Dioxide (CO2) gas. These trapped bubbles of CO2 gas expand during baking, making cakes and breads rise and become soft and spongy.
DECOY BUSTING: Sodium carbonate is Washing Soda (used in laundry). Sodium hydroxide is Caustic Soda (a very strong base used to make soap and clear drains). Calcium hypochlorite is Bleaching Powder (used to disinfect water).
EXAM INSIGHT: Baking soda is also a primary ingredient in dry-chemical fire extinguishers (because heating it releases CO2, which smothers fires) and is used as an antacid for indigestion.

questions.stem: Bronze is a historically significant alloy. What are its two primary constituent metals?

options.option_text: Copper and Tin
Copper and Zinc
Iron and Carbon
Lead and Tin

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Bronze is an alloy consisting primarily of Copper (usually around 88%) and Tin (around 12%). Adding tin to copper makes it significantly harder, less brittle, and more resistant to corrosion than pure copper. This was such a monumental technological leap for human civilization that an entire era is named after it (The Bronze Age, which includes the Indus Valley Civilization).
DECOY BUSTING: Copper and Zinc make Brass (often used in musical instruments and decorative items). Iron and Carbon make Steel. Lead and Tin make Solder (used for melting and joining electrical wires).
EXAM INSIGHT: Distinguishing between Bronze (Copper + Tin) and Brass (Copper + Zinc) is a very common trap in exams. A mnemonic: 'Z' in Zinc does NOT go with 'Z' in Bronze.

questions.stem: Why are modern synthetic detergents better than traditional soaps for washing clothes in 'hard water'?

options.option_text: Detergents do not form insoluble scum with the calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water
Detergents are strong acids that dissolve the minerals in hard water
Soaps are completely insoluble in cold water, whereas detergents only work in cold water
Detergents contain bleaching agents that turn the hard water white

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Hard water contains high concentrations of dissolved Calcium (Ca2+) and Magnesium (Mg2+) ions. When traditional soap is used in hard water, these ions react with the soap molecules to form an insoluble, sticky white precipitate called 'scum'. This wastes soap and leaves clothes looking dull. Synthetic detergents are chemically different (they are salts of sulfonic acids); they remain soluble in hard water and do not form scum, continuing to lather and clean effectively.
DECOY BUSTING: Detergents are not strong acids (they would destroy clothes). Both soap and detergents dissolve in cold water, but detergents perform better overall. Detergents may contain bleach, but that has nothing to do with solving the 'hard water' problem.
EXAM INSIGHT: While detergents are superior cleaners, they have an environmental drawback. Many early synthetic detergents contained phosphates, which caused massive algal blooms (eutrophication) in lakes and rivers, leading to their ban in many countries.

questions.stem: Which gas is dissolved under pressure in commercially bottled soda water to produce the characteristic effervescence when the bottle is opened?

options.option_text: Carbon dioxide (CO₂), which forms carbonic acid in water
Oxygen (O₂), present in air at about 21% by volume
Nitrogen (N₂), the most abundant gas in the atmosphere
Hydrogen (H₂), the lightest known element by atomic mass

questions.explanation: CO₂ is correct because it dissolves in water under high pressure to form carbonic acid (H₂CO₃); when the cap is removed and pressure drops, CO₂ escapes as bubbles. Nitrogen is used in some craft beers to give a creamier texture but does not produce the same vigorous effervescence, making it the most tempting wrong choice.

questions.stem: Which chemical compound is added to municipal drinking water supplies as a disinfectant to eliminate harmful microorganisms?

options.option_text: Sodium chloride (NaCl), commonly known as table salt
Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), a mild alkaline white powder
Sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), a chlorine-releasing compound
Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), found naturally in limestone rock

questions.explanation: Sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) releases hypochlorous acid (HOCl) in water, which destroys bacterial cell membranes and is effective as a disinfectant at very low concentrations. Sodium chloride (NaCl) is the most common distractor because both contain sodium and chlorine, but NaCl has no disinfectant property — it is simply common salt used in food.

questions.stem: LPG cylinders used for domestic cooking in Indian households primarily contain a mixture of which two hydrocarbons in liquefied form?

options.option_text: Methane and ethane, the lightest alkanes of the paraffin series
Propane and butane, both saturated members of the alkane family
Ethylene and propylene, unsaturated hydrocarbons of the alkene series
Pentane and hexane, higher alkanes used mainly as industrial solvents

questions.explanation: LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) is a mixture of propane (C₃H₈) and butane (C₄H₁₀), which can be compressed into liquid form at moderate pressures for easy storage. Methane (natural gas / PNG) is the most common distractor because it is also a domestic fuel, but it cannot be easily liquefied at room temperature and is supplied through pipelines, not cylinders.

questions.stem: Silver ornaments gradually develop a black coating on prolonged exposure to air. Which chemical compound is primarily responsible for this blackening?

options.option_text: Silver oxide (Ag₂O), formed by direct reaction with atmospheric oxygen
Silver chloride (AgCl), a white light-sensitive precipitate compound
Silver sulfide (Ag₂S), formed by reaction with sulfur compounds in air
Silver carbonate (Ag₂CO₃), produced by reaction with atmospheric CO₂

questions.explanation: Silver tarnish is black Ag₂S (silver sulfide), formed when silver reacts with trace amounts of hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) and other sulfur compounds naturally present in air. Silver oxide (Ag₂O) is the most common distractor — it is dark brown, not black, and forms only at elevated temperatures; ordinary atmospheric oxygen at room temperature does not tarnish silver appreciably.

questions.stem: Non-stick cookware coated with PTFE (Teflon) prevents food from sticking to its surface. What chemical property of PTFE is primarily responsible for this behaviour?

options.option_text: Extreme chemical inertness and very low surface energy of C–F bonds
High thermal conductivity distributing heat uniformly across the surface
Melting point above 600°C preventing deformation under cooking temperatures
Micro-porous texture that channels oils into the surface for lubrication

questions.explanation: PTFE owes its non-stick nature to the C–F bond, one of the strongest in organic chemistry, which makes it chemically inert and gives it one of the lowest surface energies (~18 mN/m) of any solid material — food molecules cannot form adhesive interactions with it. The high-melting-point option is a plausible distractor, but PTFE's melting point is ~327°C (not 600°C); non-sticking is about surface energy, not thermal stability.

questions.stem: During the saponification process used to manufacture soap, a triglyceride (fat/oil) reacts with a strong alkali such as NaOH. What are the two products formed?

options.option_text: Free fatty acid and glycerol, with NaOH acting only as a catalyst
Soap (sodium salt of fatty acid) and ethanol, via transesterification
Fatty acid and water, with glycerol separated only under acidic conditions
Soap (sodium salt of fatty acid) and glycerol, via alkaline ester hydrolysis

questions.explanation: Saponification: triglyceride + 3NaOH → 3 RCOONa (soap) + C₃H₅(OH)₃ (glycerol). The alkali hydrolyses the ester linkages AND simultaneously neutralises the free fatty acids to form their sodium salts (soap). The first option is a classic distractor — free fatty acid + glycerol is the product of acid hydrolysis, not alkaline saponification, and NaOH is a reactant, not a catalyst.

questions.stem: Aqua regia (1:3 ratio of conc. HNO₃ and conc. HCl) can dissolve gold, which resists most acids. Which reactive species generated in this mixture actually attacks the gold surface?

options.option_text: Nitrous acid (HNO₂) formed by partial reduction of nitric acid molecules
Nitrosyl chloride (NOCl) and nascent chlorine, both powerful oxidising agents
Chlorine gas (Cl₂) produced solely by oxidation of HCl by concentrated HNO₃
Perchloric acid (HClO₄) formed by rearrangement of the two mixed acids

questions.explanation: The reaction HNO₃ + 3HCl → NOCl + 2[Cl] + 2H₂O generates nitrosyl chloride (NOCl) and nascent (atomic) chlorine [Cl]; both are far stronger oxidising agents than molecular Cl₂ and together oxidise gold to Au³⁺, which is then stabilised as the chloroaurate complex [AuCl₄]⁻. Molecular chlorine gas (Cl₂) alone is a plausible distractor because HNO₃ does oxidise HCl, but Cl₂ by itself cannot dissolve gold — it is the atomic/nascent form and NOCl that do the actual work.
